youtube.title: He Can Do Anything in GTA 6. He Still Stops at Red Lights #Shorts
youtube.description:
He can do anything in GTA 6. And he still stops at every red light.

He's not alone: a PC Gamer writer posted "Help: I can't stop obeying traffic laws in GTA 6". Why won't your hands break the rules, even in a game? Because a lot of what you do isn't a choice. It's a habit.

In two diary studies, Wood, Quinn & Kashy (2002) had students write down what they were doing, hour by hour. In one study about 43% of their actions were habits (35% in the other): done almost every day, usually in the same place, often while thinking about something else. A habit is a shortcut: the cue appears, the action follows. Red light, foot on the brake. Like typing your password without thinking.

So, what do you do on autopilot?

Sources:
- PC Gamer (2026-11-19), "Help: I can't stop obeying traffic laws in GTA 6" (headline quoted): https://www.pcgamer.com/games/grand-theft-auto/help-i-cant-stop-obeying-traffic-laws-in-gta-6/
- Wood, Quinn & Kashy (2002), Habits in everyday life, JPSP 83(6): https://dornsife.usc.edu/wendy-wood/wp-content/uploads/sites/183/2023/10/Wood.Quinn_.Kashy_.2002_Habits_in_everyday_life.pdf
